### Symbols for system design

Symbols marked † are the subject's standard symbols and also have another meaning in a shared table or in another
tutorial. The conventions section of the System Design notation page lists each one with its meaning in that tutorial
and says how the two meanings are told apart where they meet.

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $A$ †, $A_i$ | steady-state availability of a system and of its component $i$: the long-run fraction of time it is up |
| $\mathrm{MTTF}$, $\mathrm{MTTR}$ | mean time to failure and mean time to repair; $A = \mathrm{MTTF}/(\mathrm{MTTF} + \mathrm{MTTR})$ |
| $\Delta$ | a period of time: a measurement window, the retention period of stored data, the freshness lifetime (TTL) of a cached response, or the period of short polling |
| $\mathrm{SLA}$, $\mathrm{SLO}$ | service level agreement (a contractual target with a remedy) and service level objective (an internal target) |
| $n$ † | number of components of a system, of replicas in a redundant group, or of servers a request fans out to |
| $T$ † | response (sojourn) time of a request: from its arrival to the end of its service |
| $t_q$ | the $q$-quantile of a latency, $t_q = \inf\{t : \mathbb P(T \leq t) \geq q\}$, so $\mathbb P(T \leq t_q) = q$ for a continuous law; the p99 latency is $t_{0.99}$ |
| $\tau_i$, $\varepsilon_i$ † | latency budget of stage $i$ of a request path, and the probability $\mathbb P(T_i > \tau_i)$ that the stage exceeds it |
| $U$ † | number of daily active users |
| $\nu_o$ † | mean number of requests of operation $o$ per active user per day |
| $\kappa$ † | peak factor: the ratio of the peak request rate to the mean rate |
| $s_o$ † | mean size in bytes of the payload of one request of operation $o$ |
| $D$ † | volume of stored data after a retention period, replicas included |
| $\beta$ † | bandwidth: bytes per second through an interface |
| $\phi_i$, $\Phi$ † | error factors of an estimate: $x/\phi \leq \hat x \leq \phi x$ |
| $\mathrm{TCO}$, $\mathrm{CapEx}$, $\mathrm{OpEx}$ | total cost of ownership; capital and operating expenses |
| $\mathrm{RTT}$ | round-trip time between two machines: from sending a short message to receiving the immediate reply |
| $t_{\mathrm{srv}}$ | server time: from the arrival of a complete request to the sending of the first byte of its response |
| $X_j$ | number of requests (or sessions) assigned to server $j$ of a pool |
| $d$ † | number of servers sampled by the power-of-$d$-choices rule of a load balancer |
| $\Delta_h$ | interval between the health-check probes of a load balancer |
| $h$ † | hit ratio of a cache: the long-run fraction of requests answered from a fresh stored response |
| $b$ † | page size of a paginated operation |
| $N_e(T)$ | number of events generated for a client in $(0, T]$ |
| $\theta$ † | timeout of a held long-poll request |
| $\Delta_{\mathrm{hb}}$ | interval between heartbeats |
| $\ell$ † | lifetime of an access token |
| $N(t)$ † | counting process: the number of arrivals in $(0, t]$; a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$ when $N(t) \sim \operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda t)$ with independent increments |
| $\lambda$ † | arrival rate (requests per unit time) |
| $\mu$ † | service rate of one server; the mean service time is $1/\mu$ |
| $c$ † | number of servers of a queue |
| $\rho$ † | utilisation (traffic intensity), $\rho = \lambda/(c\mu)$; $\rho = \lambda/\mu$ for one server |
| $a$ | offered load in erlangs, $a = \lambda/\mu$ |
| $Q(t)$, $\pi_n$ | number of requests in the system at time $t$ (waiting or in service); its stationary probabilities $\pi_n = \lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb P(Q(t) = n)$ |
| $L$ †, $L_q$ | mean number of requests in the system and in the queue |
| $W$ †, $W_q$ | mean time in the system and mean waiting time in the queue, as in Little's law $L = \lambda W$ |
| $\mathrm{M/M/1}$, $\mathrm{M/M/}c$ | Kendall's notation: arrival process / service-time distribution / number of servers (M: Markovian, that is Poisson arrivals or exponential service) |
| $C(c, a)$ † | Erlang C: the probability that an arriving request waits, in an M/M/$c$ queue with offered load $a$ |
| $\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$ | exponential distribution of rate $\lambda$: $\mathbb P(Y > t) = e^{-\lambda t}$ |
| $X$ † | throughput: completed requests per unit time |
| $T_{(j)}$, $\hat t_q$ | order statistics of $n$ measured response times, and the empirical $q$-quantile $\hat t_q = T_{(\lceil qn\rceil)}$ |
| $T_q$ † | waiting time of a request before its service begins, with mean $W_q$ |
| $M$ †, $Z$ † | number of users of a closed system and their mean think time |
| $D_k$, $D$ †, $D_{\max}$ | service demand of resource $k$ (busy time per completed request), the total demand $D = \sum_kD_k$, and the largest |
| $\rho_k$ | utilisation of resource $k$ |
| $M^*$ | knee population of a closed system, $M^* = (D + Z)/D_{\max}$ |
| $N$ † | replication factor: the number of replicas of a data item |
| $R$ †, $W$ † | read and write quorum sizes: the replicas that must answer a read, and acknowledge a write |
| $e \to e'$ † | happens-before: event $e$ may causally affect event $e'$ |
| $e \parallel e'$ | concurrency: neither $e \to e'$ nor $e' \to e$ |
| $C(e)$ † | Lamport timestamp of event $e$ |
| $V(e)$, $V(e)[i]$ | vector timestamp of event $e$ and its component for process $i$; $V \leq V'$ componentwise, $V < V'$ when also $V \neq V'$ |
| $h : U \to [0, 1)$ | hash function onto the ring of consistent hashing, positions read modulo 1 |
| $K$, $v$ | number of keys; number of virtual nodes per physical node |
| $e_1, e_2, \dots$ † | entries of a replication log, applied in order by every replica |
| $k$ †, $f$ † | followers whose acknowledgement a semi-synchronous leader waits for, and the number of followers |
| $G$, $S$ † | length of one arc of a hash ring, and a node's share: the total length of the arcs it owns |
| $D$ †, $q$ † | bound on the delivery delay of a heartbeat, and the probability that a heartbeat is lost |
| $T_{\mathrm{fail}}$ | period without a counter increase after which gossip membership considers a member failed |
| $H$ † | number of heartbeats sent in a period |
| $b$ †, $N_b$, $P_{\mathrm{col}}$ | random bits of an identifier, the $N_b = 2^b$ possible values, and the probability that two of $n$ identifiers collide |
| $\mathrm{inv}(o)$, $\mathrm{res}(o)$, $o \prec o'$ | invocation and response times of an operation, and real-time precedence: $\mathrm{res}(o) < \mathrm{inv}(o')$ |
| $G_1$, $G_2$ † | the two sides of a network partition |
| $t_{\mathrm{msg}}$ | delivery bound of the partially synchronous model: a message arrives within $t_{\mathrm{msg}}$ or is lost |
| $f$ † | the number of processes that may fail (crash or Byzantine) |
| $(n, v)$, $n_p$ | a Paxos proposal with number $n$ and value $v$, and the highest prepare number an acceptor has answered |
| $T$ †, $U$ | Raft terms |
| $L$ †, $\rho$ † | length of a lease, and the bound on relative clock drift: one clock runs at most $1 + \rho$ times as fast as another |
| $\tau$ † | a fencing token (lock generation number) |
| $q$ † | size of a quorum |
| $t_c$, $t_s$, $t_w$ | times of a cache read, a store read and a cache write |
| $C$ † | capacity of a cache, in keys |
| $p_k$, $P_C$ | popularity of key $k$ under the independent reference model, and the total popularity of the $C$ most popular keys |
| $s$ †, $H_{K,s}$ | exponent of a Zipf law, and the normalising sum $\sum_{j \leq K}j^{-s}$ |
| $r$ †, $J$ | time to regenerate a cached value, and the width of the TTL jitter interval |
| $B(t)$ | backlog of a queue at time $t$: messages arrived and not yet processed |
| $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_0$ | arrival rates of a queue during and after a burst |
| $A(t)$ †, $D(t)$ † | arrivals and departures by time $t$ in the fluid model of a queue |
| $S$ † | number of subscriptions of a topic |
| $f_m$, $k(m)$ | effect of message $m$ on a consumer's state, and its idempotency key |
| $x(m)$, $v(m)$, $t(m)$ | key, value and version set by a versioned message $m$ |
| $N_p$, $N_c$ | number of partitions of a topic, and of consumers in a consumer group |
| $q$ †, $r$ †, $s_j$ | in the range assignment, $N_p = qN_c + r$ with $0 \leq r < N_c$, and consumer $j$'s first partition $s_j = jq + \min(j, r)$ |
| $o_c$, $o_u$ | committed offset of a partition, and its first unprocessed offset |
| $n_a$, $t_0$ | maximum number of processing attempts, and the delay before the first retry |
| $q$ †, $s$ † | probability that an attempt fails transiently, and the longest duration of an attempt |
| $n_\ell$ | number of layers that retry a failing call |
| $b$ † | number of messages in a batch |
| $\Sigma_j$, $\operatorname{apply}$ | state after the first $j$ events $e_1, \dots, e_j$ † of an event-sourced log, and the function that applies an event to a state |
| $k$ † | number of events between snapshots, or between commits of an offset |
| $\theta$ † | time to live of a message in a queue |
| $n$ † | number of participants of a distributed transaction |
| $C_i(t)$ †, $\kappa$ †, $\varepsilon$ † | reading of physical clock $i$ at physical time $t$, its drift bound $\lvert dC_i/dt - 1\rvert < \kappa$, and the skew bound $\lvert C_i(t) - C_j(t)\rvert < \varepsilon$; for TrueTime, $\varepsilon$ is half the width of an interval |
| $\mu$ †, $\tau$ †, $\xi$, $d$ † | in Lamport's synchronisation: least delay of a relation between events, interval between messages on an arc, unpredictable delay, and diameter of the network |
| $[\mathit{earliest}, \mathit{latest}]$ | the interval returned by TrueTime's $\mathrm{TT.now}()$ |
| $s$ †, $s_i$, $\varepsilon_{\max}$ | commit timestamp (of transaction $T_i$), and the largest half-width of TrueTime intervals |
| $T_i$ †, $C_i$ † | steps and compensating transactions of a saga |
| $\delta_i$, $\gamma_j$ | additive changes made by a saga's steps and by other transactions |
| $p$ † | index of a saga's pivot step |
| $f$ †, $P$, $R$ † | failure probability of a dual write's second write; period and duration of reconciliation |
| $\Delta_p$ | polling interval of an outbox relay |
| $\lambda_h$, $c$ †, $h$ † | rate of reservation holds, fraction confirmed, and length of an unconfirmed hold |
| $k$ † | number of requests contending for one item |
| $M$ †, $R$ † | numbers of map and reduce tasks of a MapReduce job |
| $P$ †, $K$ †, $\phi$ | number of intermediate pairs, of distinct intermediate keys, and the fraction of pairs with one key |
| $v_1 \oplus v_2$ | a commutative and associative merge of values, as in a combiner |
| $t_v$, $T_\infty$, $c$ † | duration of task $v$ of a DAG, length of its critical path, and number of workers |
| $N$ †, $w_j$, $S$ † | rows of a table, width in bytes of column $j$, and the set of columns a query reads |
| $d$ †, $p_i$ † | number of distinct values of a column, and the probability of value $i$ |
| $D$ †, $k$ † | number of partitions of a table, and the number a query keeps |
| $e$ †, $L$ †, $S$ †, $g$ | event time; length and slide of a window; gap of a session window |
| $m$ †, $\delta$ † | largest event time received, and the delay of a watermark $W = m - \delta$ |
| $s$ †, $X$ † | rate of a Bernoulli sample, and the number of sampled events |
| $w$ †, $d$ †, $\varepsilon$ †, $\delta$ † | width, depth, error and failure probability of a count-min sketch (as in the earlier row) |
| $a_i$, $\hat a_i$, $\lVert a\rVert_1$ | count of item $i$, its count-min estimate, and the total count |
| $p$ †, $q$ †, $m$ †, $M_j$, $c_m$ | HyperLogLog: bits choosing a register, rank bits, number of registers $m = 2^p$, value of register $j$, and the estimator's constant |
| $m$ †, $k$ †, $n$ † | Bloom filter: number of bits, of hash functions, and of inserted keys |
| $p_{\mathrm{fp}}$ | false-positive probability of a Bloom filter, $p_{\mathrm{fp}} \approx (1 - e^{-kn/m})^k$ |
| $h_1, \dots, h_k$ † | the hash functions of a Bloom filter, onto the positions $\{1, \dots, m\}$ |
| $p'$, $p$ †, $\zeta$ | Bloom filter: the probability $(1 - 1/m)^{kn}$ that a bit is still $0$, its approximation $e^{-kn/m}$, and the fraction of bits that are $0$ |
| $f$ † | the approximate false-positive rate $(1 - e^{-kn/m})^k$ of a Bloom filter, as a function of $k$ |
| $X \to Y$ † | functional dependency: rows that agree on the attributes $X$ agree on $Y$ |
| $X^+$ | closure of the attribute set $X$ under the functional dependencies |
| $\pi_S(r)$ †, $r_1 \bowtie r_2$ | projection of the relation $r$ on the attributes $S$, and natural join |
| $t$ †, $H$ † | minimum degree and height of a B-tree |
| $T_i$ †, $r_i(x)$ †, $w_i(x)$ | transaction $i$, and its read and write of the item $x$ |
| $\ell_i(x)$ †, $u_i(x)$ | acquisition and release of a lock on $x$ by $T_i$ |
| $\sigma_i$ | lock point of $T_i$: the time at which it acquires its last lock |
| $\mathcal D$, $\lvert d \rvert$ | a collection of documents, and the number of terms of a document $d$ |
| $\mathrm{tf}_{t,d}$, $\mathrm{df}_t$ | term frequency of $t$ in $d$, and document frequency of $t$ in $\mathcal D$ |
| $k_1$, $b$ † | the constants of BM25, $1.2$ and $0.75$ in SQLite |
| $w$, $d$ † | width and depth of a count-min sketch; $\varepsilon$, $\delta$ its error and failure probability |
| $b$, $r$ † | capacity and refill rate of a token bucket |

Conventions:

- Sizes and rates carry their units: $\mathrm{B}$ for bytes and $\mathrm{b}$ for bits, decimal prefixes ($1\,\mathrm{GB} =
  10^9\,\mathrm{B}$) and binary ones ($1\,\mathrm{GiB} = 2^{30}\,\mathrm{B}$), and $\mathrm{req/s}$ for requests per
  second.
- Times are in seconds unless a unit is given, with $\mathrm{ms}$ and $\mu\mathrm s$ for latencies.
